quizzes.title: Partnership Beyond the Summit: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
The relationship between India and Japan reaches back to the struggle against colonial rule. During that period, a leader of the freedom movement received Japanese backing for an army he set up to fight colonial rule, and this episode remains part of the historical link between the two countries. The 16th annual summit, held in New Delhi, is the latest meeting in a long series of engagements between the two governments, and both countries have built ties across several sectors since then.

Today the partnership spans investment, development and defence. Japan is a significant investor in India and has long supported its development through official assistance, a form of support that has been a long-standing feature of the relationship. The navies, armies and air forces of the two countries all take part in joint exercises. Cooperation has also reached space, where the two countries are working together on a lunar polar mission.

Beyond the bilateral framework, India and Japan coordinate on several global programmes, including efforts linked to solar energy and to infrastructure that can withstand disasters. They also back a trilateral initiative that strengthens supply chains with a third partner. Their engagement also sits within a wider set of maritime and regional frameworks. The partnership is also reflected in the outcomes of the summit itself.

questions.q: The army that a leader of the freedom movement set up with Japanese backing to fight colonial rule is called:
questions.explanation: The booklet names this army as Azad Hind Fauj, also called the Indian National Army.

questions.q: Which name is also used for the Lunar Polar Exploration Mission (LUPEX)?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists LUPEX as also called Chandrayaan-5.

questions.q: Japan has been India's largest Official Development Assistance donor since which year?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates Japan's position as India's largest ODA donor to 1958.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India and Japan take part in a naval exercise that also includes the United States.
Reason (R): Malabar is a naval exercise involving India, Japan, the United States and Australia.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Malabar is the naval exercise with the United States and Australia, which is why it explains the assertion.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Dharma Guardian   ->   D. Air Force
II. SHINYUU Maitri   ->   A. Multilateral naval exercise
III. JIMEX   ->   B. Army
IV. Milan   ->   C. Navy
questions.explanation: Dharma Guardian is the army exercise, SHINYUU Maitri the air force one, JIMEX the navy one and Milan the multilateral naval one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about joint exercises of India and Japan:
I. Milan is a multilateral naval exercise.
II. JIMEX is a naval exercise between India and Japan.
III. Malabar is a bilateral exercise between India and Japan alone.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Milan is multilateral and JIMEX is a naval exercise between India and Japan, while Malabar also includes the United States and Australia.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Skill-Up frameworks listed in the booklet:
I. QUAD is one of the listed frameworks.
II. BIMSTEC is one of the listed frameworks.
III. The Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure is one of the listed frameworks.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: QUAD and BIMSTEC appear under Skill-Up, while the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure is listed among global programmes.

quizzes.title: Green Hydrogen Mission: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Hydrogen exists only in combination with other elements, so it has to be extracted from naturally occurring compounds before it can be used. Its colour labels, such as grey, blue and green, are linked to how it is produced. Green hydrogen is the category made by a process that uses electricity to split hydrogen from a compound, with the electricity supplied by a particular type of source.

India has built a national mission around green hydrogen. The mission aims to bring change to several sectors, including energy, industry and mobility, and it also seeks to develop manufacturing capacity within the country. Its goals include opportunities for selling the fuel and its derivatives abroad. The mission has components that support a transition programme and a partnership between government and private players for innovation. Its expected results include a reduction in fossil fuel imports, which is measured in money terms.

Taken together, these elements show that the mission covers production, domestic manufacturing and trade rather than a single activity. Its scope therefore reaches from the process used to make the fuel to the markets in which it could be sold. This wide scope means the mission is not limited to a single step in the supply chain.

questions.q: By 2030, the national green hydrogen mission is expected to bring fossil fuel import savings of how much?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the expected 2030 fossil fuel import savings as Rs 1 lakh crore.

questions.q: Which statement about the commercial status of green hydrogen is correct?
options: It is fully commercially viable across India
It is not commercially viable at present
It is viable only for export
It is viable only in rural areas
questions.explanation: The booklet states that green hydrogen is not commercially viable at present.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership is a public-private partnership.
Reason (R): Its purpose is research and development.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the research aim does not explain why the partnership is structured as a public-private one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the mission:
I. Green hydrogen is commercially viable at present.
II. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is the nodal ministry for the mission.
III. The expected fossil fuel import savings by 2030 are measured in rupees.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Green hydrogen is not commercially viable at present, while the nodal ministry and the rupee-denominated savings are both as stated.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. SIGHT   ->   C. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
II. SHIP   ->   A. Rs 1 lakh crore
III. Nodal ministry for the mission   ->   D. Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition Programme
IV. Expected fossil fuel import savings by 2030   ->   B. Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership
questions.explanation: SIGHT is the transition programme, SHIP the innovation partnership, MNRE the nodal ministry and Rs 1 lakh crore the 2030 savings.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. SHIP is a public-private partnership for research and development.
II. The mission's nodal ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
III. SIGHT is a public-private partnership for research and development.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: SHIP is the public-private R&D partnership and the nodal ministry statement is correct, while SIGHT is a transition programme rather than a partnership.

questions.q: The electrolyser used to produce green hydrogen is powered by which kind of energy?
questions.explanation: The booklet says green hydrogen is made using an electrolyser powered by renewable energy.

questions.q: What term describes the process of splitting water with electricity to produce hydrogen? (one word)
